# Claim Types and Where Video Helps

- Workers' comp drives claim volume: ~600 claims last year, ~90 still open
- Commercial auto runs 3-4 claims/week (~150-200/year) and carries the dollars
  - Lytx cameras in every cab: live view, hard braking and distraction alerts, crash clips pushed automatically
  - Footage used heavily on auto; rarely on yard, warehouse or comp claims
- Premises and product claims round it out
  - Product claims often reach for the distributor (e.g., a contractor blames a bad batch of shingles)
- Yard and warehouse injuries: the employer takes employees at their word and rarely pulls video
  - Carrier and TPA investigate more; the employer cares about morale
  - Comp injuries are reported to the carrier right away, with no internal review first

# Safety and Loss Control

- Safety team visits each yard about once a month; site safety leads report in
  - Yards run from Arkansas to Colorado
  - Corporate safety sits next to the risk team
- Near misses are talked about but not tracked or reported
- Video for spotting hazards before an injury seen as genuinely useful
  - Bad lighting, slick loading areas
  - A camera pilot with CompScience was discussed once and dropped

# Go-to-Market View

- Warehouse cameras: value is in safety and loss control, sold to whoever runs the site
- Fleet footage: value is in claims handling, sold to carriers
  - Carriers could offer a premium percentage off to insureds who adopt
  - Reinsurers possible for the claims angle
- Lytx rolled out ~3 years ago for safety and claims visibility, not premium credit
- Targets at carriers: claims directors, VPs, AVPs, regional VPs
  - Whether a claims manager can buy depends on company size and authority setup
  - At Keystone Casualty a claims manager could not

# Next Steps

- **Line up carrier claims leaders and fleet contacts**
